description: Adds one rule to a ruleset. Use ONLY when a human explicitly asks. ONE INSTRUCTION PER RULE — if it needs "and" to join two obligations, add two rules. Choose the type carefully: "must" = comply, and stop and ask if you cannot; "must_not" = never; "prefer" = use this but fall back if genuinely unavailable — reach for this when the rule has legitimate exceptions; "consult" = read a named library when a condition applies. CONSULT IS THE MOST VALUABLE AND MOST OVERLOOKED TYPE: instead of copying a design system into rules, add one consult rule pointing at that library. The pointer costs almost nothing and is always present; the library is only fetched when the work calls for it. Always supply a `reason` when one exists — rules with a stated reason get followed more reliably and do not get deleted later as arbitrary. Do not mark a rule as checked unless a real lint rule, CI check, test or workflow gate actually blocks it. Cannot add to the workspace baseline — only a person can do that.

consultLibraryId.description: Required for a consult rule, and only for a consult rule.

reason.description: Why the rule exists. Strongly recommended.

scopeType.description: Narrow where it applies. Prefer a file path over prose when the work is file-based.

text.description: One sentence, one instruction. Max 300 characters.

type.description: See the guidance above — pick deliberately.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID. If not provided, uses your default workspace.
